patients.label: Woman with recurrent takotsubo cardiomyopathy (2014, 2015, 2018) after three earlier episodes labelled myocardial infarction

identity_evidence.quote: We present a 76-year-old woman who had likely a total of six recurrent takotsubo cardiomyopathy episodes spanning over 33 years.

attribution_limitations: The abstract and discussion state a likely total of six recurrent takotsubo episodes over 33 years, three of them confirmed (2014, 2015, 2018) and the three earlier episodes labelled myocardial infarction only possibly takotsubo.
The discussion lists three morphological types (apical, apical-to-mid-cavity, focal) without naming which presentation had the apical-to-mid-cavity type.

The text says coronary angiography showed normal coronary arteries on each occasion after listing the 1986, 1988 and 1998 episodes; the abstract confirms normal coronary arteries on each of those three occasions, but the performed procedure is only explicit for 1986 (angiogram) and stated generally for the others.
The 1998 creatine kinase is given as 233 (no unit) in the timeline and as 1.7 times the upper limit of normal in the case text; the source does not state these are the same measurement.
The 76-year-old age is stated in the sentence about the first 2014 presentation, but the case spans 33 years and the age reference time is not stated.

The discussion says the 2014 myocardial infarction exclusion instigates a potential change in past medical history and implicitly a requirement for lifelong secondary prevention; this is interpretive and no such plan is stated for the patient.

Source conflict on medicines: the supplementary slide set states she is currently managed with furosemide, ramipril and atorvastatin, while the article says she was discharged on no specific therapy; the slide gives no time and the article does not say whether discharge was from the 2018 admission or from clinic follow-up.

The case text calls the 2015 ventriculogram supportive of apical takotsubo, while the discussion lists three morphological types (apical, apical-to-mid-cavity, focal) without naming the presentation for each.

Source conflict on previous myocardial infarction: the article says cardiac MRI ruled out any current or previous myocardial infarction, while the supplementary slide set lists 3 previous myocardial infarctions in 1986, 1988 and 1998.

Hedging difference, not a conflicting value: the article calls the 2015 ventriculogram finding a "probable mild area of hypokinesis in the inferior apical wall", while the supplementary slide set states "mild hypokinesis" without "probable".
